marker_between: Arabic "between" framing -- "بين ... و ..." ("between January and March").
"بين" (bayna): W. Wright, *A Grammar of the Arabic Language*, 3rd ed., vol. II,
§46 -- بين "between", governing two coordinated terms joined by و.
Badawi, Carter & Gully, *Modern Written Arabic*, §2.9 s.v. بين.
marker_during: "fi" is the locative preposition used with months.
marker_from: Arabic range "from" lead -- opens a bounded or open interval, the correlative
of "to" (إلى) in the standard "من ... إلى ..." range framing ("from January to
March").  Written as a free word (من), never a proclitic, so it tokenizes as
"من" (min): W. Wright, *A Grammar of the Arabic Language*, 3rd ed., vol. II,
§46 (prepositions) -- من marks the starting point / origin in time and
space, correlative of إلى ("من يوم الجمعة إلى يوم الأحد").
Also: Badawi, Carter & Gully, *Modern Written Arabic: A Comprehensive Grammar*
(Routledge), §2.9 -- من ... إلى as the standard bounded-range construction.
marker_half: Arabic period noun "half" for "the first/second half of <year>" (half_period).
"نصف"/"النصف": نِصْف = أحد جزأين متساويين (Lisān al-ʿArab, root ن‑ص‑ف); the
attested surface carries the definite article ال ("النصف الأول من 2020").
marker_oclock: "الساعة" is "the hour" and names the clock, as in "الساعة الثالثة" (three
o'clock): Wiktionary, ساعة: "hour (unit of time)", "timepiece, clock, watch".  A digit hour after it
is a clock, as "at 3" is in English.
marker_to: Arabic range "to" boundary -- the term / upper limit of a bounded interval,
"إلى" (ilā): W. Wright, *A Grammar of the Arabic Language*, 3rd ed., vol. II,
§46 -- إلى marks the end point / limit reached ("إلى يوم الأحد"), correlative
of من.  Badawi, Carter & Gully, *Modern Written Arabic*, §2.9.
"الى": the same preposition written without the hamza, a ubiquitous
orthographic variant (mirrors marker_until.voc, which lists both forms).

named_day_-2: The reversed word order is as ordinary as the fronted one and was the form
that failed: "أمس الأول" matched only "أمس" (yesterday) and left "الأول"
stranded, so the day before yesterday answered YESTERDAY.  ar.wikipedia
running prose: "عقدوا أمس الأول اجتماعاً في عكا" (عملية الخالصة), "أقامت
إدارة التعليم بمحافظة ينبع أمس الأول احتفالا" (1998 في السعودية), "كأنها
جرت أمس الأول" (طاهر أبو زيد).  The undotted spelling follows this
locale's own convention of listing both.
